finding: STRUCTURAL — not a live exploit payload
summary: Every PreToolUse guard hook (bash-egress-guard.sh, mcp-guard.sh, block-dangerous-cmds.sh, protect-sensitive-reads.sh, confirm-token-required.sh, lib/deny.sh) calls `jq` by bare name. The shebang is #!/bin/bash; no hook pins PATH or resolves jq via an absolute path before calling it. If a model-controlled Bash command runs early enough in the session to prepend a writable directory to PATH (e.g. export PATH=/tmp/evil:$PATH), a subsequent tool call that triggers a guard would invoke the attacker's `jq` binary instead of /opt/homebrew/bin/jq. The fake jq could (a) emit an allow response regardless of input, (b) silently suppress the deny output, or (c) echo malformed JSON causing the hook to exit non-zero, which under bash's set -uo pipefail causes the hook to FAIL (exit 1) rather than deny. Claude Code treats a hook exit != 0 and exit != 2 as a non-blocking error in some contexts — behavior needs operator verification. lib/deny.sh itself calls `jq -n` bare: if deny.sh's jq is shadowed, the deny JSON is never emitted.
hooks_affected: ~/.claude/hooks/protect-sensitive-reads.sh (jq bare at lines 26,48-50, command -v jq check at line 47)
~/.claude/hooks/lib/deny.sh (jq -n bare at line 5 — the canonical deny emitter)
